name: PCI magnetic wire
full_name: Magnetically steerable PCI guidewire with a Helmholtz-coil EMA and a motorized feeding stage
group: J.-O. Park, S. Park, C.-S. Kim, Chonnam National University and Korea Medical Microrobot Center
versions: 2017: two pairs of Helmholtz coils + motorized feeding stage, feed-forward + PID steering (jeong2017_feasibility); 2019: EMA of two Helmholtz pairs and one Maxwell pair (one x-axis pair used) + linear-stage feeder, path regeneration, feeding control and vision tracking (kim2019_novel); 2018-21: same group's guide-wired helical microrobot (GHM) for mechanical atherectomy: 3D-printed corkscrew head (1.6 x 9.5 mm, NdFeB magnet magnetised across the axis) on a spherical joint at the tip of a 0.152 mm nitinol guidewire, steered by a uniform field and spun for drilling by a rotating field (18-370 Hz, resonant circuits) of three Helmholtz-coil pairs (30 mT), advanced and retracted by a motorised linear-stage feeder in an automatic tracing mode; in vitro feasibility (Nguyen 2018 EMBC); phantom path tracking, gelatin-thrombus drilling and 5 rats in vivo (Nguyen 2021 IEEE TBME 68:2490-2498, Secs. II-IV, Figs. 2, 4) (Konda 2025 Table 2 row 8) (nguyen2021_guidewired; konda2025_robotically)
target_anatomy: coronary (PCI), tested in planar vessel phantoms; 2021: chronic total occlusion; rat abdominal aorta used as a coronary-size model (nguyen2021_guidewired Sec. IV-G)
devices_driven: 2017: Asahi Conquest Pro 12 guidewire (tip OD 0.23 mm) with a bullet-shaped NdFeB magnet 1 mm x 7 mm (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 2.1); 2019: 0.2 mm nitinol wire with a magnet tip (kim2019_novel Sec. 4.1); 2021: 0.152 mm super-elastic nitinol guidewire (Confluent Medical) carrying the 3D-printed helical head; 130 mm of wire through a Tygon sheath (0.79 mm ID) as guiding catheter (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. II-A, IV-A)
n_dof_detail: 2: insertion (feeder) + planar tip steering (field); 2021: insertion (feeder) + 3-D steering and spin of the head (field)
translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (motorized feeding stage with a guidewire holder, jeong2017_feasibility abstract; linear stage, kim2019_novel Fig. 1); tip steered magnetically
rotation_detail: field direction of the Helmholtz coils (no shaft rotation); 2021: a rotating field spins the helical head on its spherical joint; the guidewire does not turn (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. II-A, III)
footprint_mm: Helmholtz coil radius 162 mm, region of interest 100 x 100 (kim2019_novel Sec. 2.1)
imaging_compat: overhead CCD camera only (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 3.1; kim2019_novel); 2021: optical camera on the phantom, C-arm X-ray (Ziehm Vision RFD) in the rat study (nguyen2021_guidewired Sec. IV-A)
validation_detail: 2017: five-branch phantom (about 4 mm branches), insertion success 100% with feed-forward + PID vs about 75% with feed-forward only (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 3.3); 2019: smooth and sharply curved vessel phantoms, 3 paths x 3 replicates (kim2019_novel Sec. 4, Table 1); 2021: 5 rats in vivo (abdominal aorta, injected 9 % gelatin thrombus, contrast angiography): thrombus drilled without perforation in 3, blood flow restored in 2, rats 1 and 2 died during thrombus formation and rat 3 of bleeding after drilling; vessel phantom path tracking RMSE about 0.2 mm, maximum below 0.7 mm at 0.3 mm/s; gelatin thrombi in tubes drilled through, 54 mm (9 %) in about 48 s and 40 mm (11 %) in 43 s (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. IV-D to IV-G, Table II, Figs. 6-8)
key_numbers: steering-angle error below 0.5 deg with PID vs about 7 deg feed-forward only (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 3.2); tip-position RMSE 0.44 +/- 0.19 mm on path I, below 0.7 +/- 0.4 mm on all paths; feeding speed 1 mm/s; camera 0.1 mm per pixel (kim2019_novel Sec. 3-4); 2021: three Helmholtz pairs on three 15 kW supplies, 30 mT, rotating field up to 370 Hz; drilling force up to 0.8 N and torque 0.1125 mN m at 100 Hz; feedback steering error below 0.5 deg (maximum 0.52 deg) against about 3 deg feed-forward (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. III, IV-A, IV-D)
